QF.id: VIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_39

question.text: When the Nifty futures contract is trading at a discount to the spot Nifty index (i.e., futures price < spot price), the market is said to be in:

answer.text: Backwardation, which can occur when expected dividends are high or when there is strong bearish sentiment
Contango, which is the normal state of the market reflecting positive cost of carry
Arbitrage equilibrium, indicating that the market is fairly priced
Basis risk, indicating that the hedge will not be effective

explanation.text: The Logic: Backwardation occurs when the futures price is below the spot price, so the basis (Spot - Futures) is positive. In equity futures this can arise when the expected dividend yield q exceeds the financing rate r (so q > r in the cost-of-carry formula), or when expectations are bearish and speculators aggressively sell futures. The Trap: Contango is when futures price is above spot price, not below it. Backwardation is a market condition describing the price relationship, not a measure of hedge effectiveness. Note: Page 48 of the Series VIII workbook defines backwardation as futures price lower than spot price; page 45 supports the q > r condition under which futures trade at a discount.
